title: Strict localization of a closed subscheme is the base change of the ambient strict localization
statement: Let $i:Z\to W$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] and let $\bar a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $Z_{(\bar a)}$ and $W_{(i\bar a)}$ be the strict localizations of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with structural morphisms $j_Z:Z_{(\bar a)}\to Z$ and $j_W:W_{(i\bar a)}\to W$, and let $h:Z_{(\bar a)}\to W_{(i\bar a)}$ be the spectrum of the unique local ring homomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3) for $g=i$, so that $j_W\circ h=i\circ j_Z$. Then the morphism $(j_Z,h):Z_{(\bar a)}\to Z\times_WW_{(i\bar a)}$ into the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] is an isomorphism. Equivalently, if $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq W$ is an affine open [def-weil-affine-spectrum] containing the image of $i\bar a$ and $i^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, then the ring homomorphism $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{W,i\bar a}\to\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Z,\bar a}$ defining $h$ is surjective with kernel $I\,\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{W,i\bar a}$. No Noetherian or reducedness hypothesis is made; nilpotents of $Z$ are retained.

source.place: Tag 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization), proved as a special case of Tag 05WR (lemma-quasi-finite-strict-henselization), whose statement identifies the strict henselization through the functorial diagram of Tag 04GU (lemma-strictly-henselian-functorial); scheme form via the affine chart of the closed immersion.

proof.text: Choose an affine open U = Spec A containing the image of the geometric point. Its inverse image under i is a closed subscheme of Spec A, so the affine closed-immersion quotient criterion gives an ideal I and an isomorphism with Spec(A/I). The one-point source Spec Ω factors through this inverse image, giving x with a = x followed by the quotient chart k. Let p be the image of x in Spec A, and use the geometric residue embedding κ(p) → Ω induced by x. Apply [lem-trf-strict-local-closed-chart-map] to this actual Cartesian quotient chart. It gives the chart maps α:A → C and β:A/I → D, where C and D are the ambient and closed strict-local coordinate rings, together with the local quotient bases R and S=R/J, J=IR, compatible pointed presentations, and the canonical local map u:C → D. Both structural morphisms factor through the charts, u is R-linear with residue map id_K, and the specified local S-algebra map d:C/IC → D satisfies d q = u.

source.place: Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), affine-neighbourhood and residue-triples comparison; compatibility of the induced map with algebra.tex Tag 04GU (lemma-strictly-henselian-functorial).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-pointed-etale-small-filtered] to the two pointed-etale presentations of [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Reindex each universal cocone by a small equivalent category and transport its vertex along the recorded algebra identification. This exhibits C as an ind-etale R-algebra and D as an ind-etale S-algebra. The local quotient S is nontrivial, so J is proper and hence J ⊆ m_R. The chart-data residue equations give agreement of the two base residue maps and identify their common kernel with m_R; the latter follows because R → K factors through R/m_R followed by a field embedding. Apply [lem-trf-ind-etale-quotient-two-base-inverse] to the actual u, using its locality and residue compatibility. It gives surjectivity of u and ker u=JC. The equality (IR)C=IC follows from composition of ideal extension and the chart-base equation. Since d q=u and q is surjective, d is surjective. If d(q(c))=d(q(c′)), then u(c-c′)=0, hence c-c′ lies in IC; thus q(c)=q(c′). Therefore the specified d is bijective, independently of the quotient algebra structure selected by the inverse theorem.

source.place: Tag 08HR (lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit), applied over S twice and R once, following the inverse-composite argument of Tag 08HT (lemma-uniqueness-henselian).

proof.text: The quotient base-change identity [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] gives the pushout square A → A/I, A → C, with vertex C/IC. In Lean use the proved source-library CommRingCat.isPushout_quotient and apply Spec, the affine fibre-product principle of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Transport the vertex by the ring isomorphism d of Step 2. Its composite with C → C/IC is u by the recorded factorization. Its composite with A/I → C/IC is β: after precomposing the surjection A → A/I this is exactly uα=βq_I, which follows from the two local-base equations and the R-linearity of u in Step 1. Thus this is a pullback square with top map Spec β and left map Spec u. Paste horizontally with the original quotient-chart pullback [lem-trf-strict-local-closed-chart-map]. The structural chart equations identify the outer square with j_Z, h, i and j_W, because Spec u is the prescribed strictHenselizationMap by full faithfulness of Spec. The comparison into the chosen pullback [def-pc-fibre-product] agrees with the pullback-square isomorphism on both projections, so it is an isomorphism. No Noetherian or reducedness hypothesis was used.
